settings.headline: Your recovery isn't a product. It's an equation.
settings.subheadline: Alcohol doesn't just cost you a morning — it costs you the executive function you get paid for. Acetaldehyde builds faster than your liver clears it, sleep architecture fragments even through eight hours, and neurotransmitters take days to rebuild. Which of those is your bottleneck depends entirely on how you drink, how often, and what your body does about it.

settings.title: Timing changes the entire protocol.
settings.body: Before a night out, the goal is buffering the pathway that clears acetaldehyde while it is being produced. The next morning that window has closed and the goal is replenishment instead. Same body, two different formulations — a static product can only be right half the time.

settings.title: Frequency changes the target.
settings.body: Twice a month is an acute event. Four nights a week is a chronic metabolic load, and the pressure moves off your morning and onto your liver's methylation and glutathione capacity. The person who needs the second protocol usually thinks they need the first.

settings.title: Your bottleneck isn't everyone's bottleneck.
settings.body: For some people it is cognitive — the fog and the flat affect that outlast the morning. For others it is gastrointestinal, and nothing else matters until that is handled. For others there is no acute symptom at all, which is exactly the profile where long-term load goes unmanaged.

settings.heading: Why one-size-fits-all supplements fail you specifically
settings.intro:
Walk into any store and you'll find the same answer sold to everyone: an electrolyte packet.

Electrolytes solve dehydration. Dehydration is the least interesting thing alcohol does to a high-output brain.
settings.closer:
Three different bottlenecks. Three different protocols. One product cannot serve all three.

So we don't ask you to choose. We diagnose. The assessment maps your social calendar, your recovery speed, your cognitive demands and your GI sensitivity, then identifies which system is actually rate-limiting for you.

settings.title: The 60-second assessment
settings.body:
We map the inputs, not the symptoms. How often you're out. How hard the next morning hits. What your work demands of your brain the following day. How your gut handles it. Whether you're optimizing for tomorrow or for the next twenty years.

No medical history, no lab work, no upsell disguised as a quiz. Every question exists because the answer changes what we would send you — if it didn't, we wouldn't ask it.

settings.title: Protocol precision matching
settings.body:
Your answers route you to the protocol that fits. Party Pack to pre-load and buffer the load while it is happening. Party Recovery where the cost shows up afterwards, in the fog and the gut. Liver Detox for sustained metabolic load, where the acute symptoms are mild but the cumulative burden is the real risk.

Whichever one you match to arrives pre-sorted into daily rolls — one packet, one day, already sorted. No pill organizer, no fourteen bottles.
